statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-42258 (GHSA-75xq-5h9v-w6px): before net-imap 0.4.24, 0.5.14 and 0.6.4, Symbol arguments, which Net::IMAP sends as IMAP system flags, are written to the socket without validation, so a Symbol built from caller-supplied input can contain spaces or CRLF and inject further IMAP commands: https://github.com/ruby/net-imap/security/advisories/GHSA-75xq-5h9v-w6px. On the 0.5 release line it is fixed in net-imap 0.5.14, whose release notes name this advisory: https://github.com/ruby/net-imap/releases/tag/v0.5.14. In the DHI Alpine 3.23 repository, net-imap ships in the ruby3.4-net-imap package, which is built from the ruby-3.4 source with its own version number; ruby-3.4-full depends on it. We downloaded every published ruby3.4-net-imap package for Alpine 3.23 on x86_64 and aarch64, checked each against its repository index checksum, and compared its installed lib directory with the net-imap release from rubygems.org; each matches its release byte for byte: 0.5.8-r0 and 0.5.8-r1 install net-imap 0.5.8, 0.5.8-r2 installs net-imap 0.5.14, and 0.5.15-r2, 0.5.15-r3 and 0.5.15-r4 install net-imap 0.5.15. Each ruby-3.4 build is built together with the ruby3.4-net-imap package of the same package release (-rN): 3.4.8-r0 to 3.4.9-r1 with net-imap 0.5.8 (ruby3.4-net-imap 0.5.8-r0 and 0.5.8-r1); 3.4.9-r2, which upgrades the bundled net-imap to 0.5.14, with ruby3.4-net-imap 0.5.8-r2; and 3.4.10-r2 and every later build, whose Ruby releases bundle net-imap 0.5.15, with ruby3.4-net-imap 0.5.15-r2 to 0.5.15-r4 (0.5.15-r2 was published with ruby-3.4 3.4.10-r2). The published DHI Ruby 3.4.9 and 3.4.10 dev images for Alpine 3.23 install ruby-3.4 3.4.9-r2 with ruby3.4-net-imap 0.5.8-r2 (net-imap 0.5.14) and ruby-3.4 3.4.10-r3 with ruby3.4-net-imap 0.5.15-r3 (net-imap 0.5.15), on amd64 and arm64. The ruby-3.4-libs 3.4.9-r2 package also carries the net-imap 0.5.14 gem archive, identical to the rubygems.org file; ruby-3.4-libs 3.4.9-r1 carries none. So the first published ruby-3.4 build that ships the fix is 3.4.9-r2: the builds before it ship net-imap 0.5.8, and it and every later build ship net-imap 0.5.14 or 0.5.15.

CVE-2026-42258 (GHSA-75xq-5h9v-w6px): in the Ruby net-imap gem, Net::IMAP sends Symbol arguments to the server without validating them, so an application that builds a Symbol from untrusted input can be made to send additional IMAP commands (command injection): https://github.com/ruby/net-imap/security/advisories/GHSA-75xq-5h9v-w6px. Upstream fixed it in net-imap 0.4.24 on the 0.4 line, 0.5.14 on the 0.5 line and 0.6.4 on the 0.6 line; the 0.6.4 release notes list GHSA-75xq-5h9v-w6px: https://github.com/ruby/net-imap/releases/tag/v0.6.4. The DHI ruby-4.0 package for Alpine 3.23 is published as 4.0.1-r0, 4.0.1-r1, 4.0.2-r1, 4.0.2-r2, 4.0.3-r2, 4.0.4-r2, 4.0.4-r3, 4.0.5-r3, 4.0.6-r3, 4.0.6-r4, 4.0.7-r4, 4.0.9-r4, 4.0.10-r4 and 4.0.10-r5, for x86_64 and aarch64. It ships net-imap in its ruby4.0-net-imap gem package, which carries the gem's version rather than Ruby's, so the range below is written in the ruby-4.0 package's own versions, and each ruby-4.0 build is placed by the net-imap its ruby4.0-net-imap package installs. The gem package keeps the gem's own version but takes its -rN release number from the Ruby build that produced it, and the repository keeps one copy of each package version, so the gem package versions published under a given -rN are exactly the net-imap releases the Ruby builds with that -rN shipped. We read Net::IMAP::VERSION in lib/net/imap.rb of every published ruby4.0-net-imap package for both architectures, each verified against the repository index checksum, and listed the contents of every published ruby-4.0-libs package: the published ruby4.0-net-imap packages are 0.6.2-r0, 0.6.2-r1, 0.6.2-r2, 0.6.2-r3, 0.6.4.1-r3, 0.6.4.1-r4 and 0.6.4.1-r5. 0.6.2-r0, -r1 and -r2 install net-imap 0.6.2, the only gem version under -r0, -r1 and -r2, so 4.0.1-r0 through 4.0.4-r2 ship 0.6.2. Under -r3 two gem versions exist: 0.6.2-r3, which despite its label installs net-imap 0.6.4, and 0.6.4.1-r3, which installs net-imap 0.6.4.1. The 4.0.4-r3 and 4.0.5-r3 builds are the ones that replaced their bundled net-imap with 0.6.4: ruby-4.0-libs 4.0.4-r3 and 4.0.5-r3 both carry the net-imap-0.6.4 gem archive that install left behind, while no other ruby-4.0-libs build carries a net-imap archive; 4.0.6-r3 ships 0.6.4.1. 0.6.4.1-r4 and 0.6.4.1-r5 install net-imap 0.6.4.1, so 4.0.6-r4, 4.0.7-r4, 4.0.9-r4, 4.0.10-r4 and 4.0.10-r5 ship 0.6.4.1. Both architectures agree for every build. Every ruby-4.0 build before 4.0.4-r3 ships a net-imap without this fix, and 4.0.4-r3 is the first that ships net-imap 0.6.4, so the range is introduced at the first published build and fixed at 4.0.4-r3.
